title: Basement / corridor dressing concepts
summary: Owner-accepted modeling direction, 12 November 2026. Four fresh native PIE captures and three generated dressing proposals. N = new production work, R = existing mesh reuse, V = material variant. Agent production records the requested OpenCode worker and current launch state. Concepts are not implemented models.

items.title: A / Junction — generated dressing proposal
items.alt: Generated proposal on new junction gameplay: utility pipes, analog cabinet, work orders, olive lower wall paint and existing low janitor cart
items.body:
**Owner accepted this direction for modeling on 12 November 2026. Meshes remain unimplemented/unreviewed.**

**AI CONCEPT / not placed in Unreal.** Built on the new native junction capture after walking. The architecture, openings and route remain the basis.

**NEW:** N01 pipe kit across the upper left wall and around the pier; N02 conduit along the upper right wall; N03 analog cabinet on the left wall; N04 EQUIPMENT plaque at the right corridor entrance; N05 work-order panel on the central face. **REUSE:** R01 low Janitor_Cart, far left. **VARIANT:** V01 olive lower-wall paint and controlled wear.

**Locate the props** (x/y from top left): cabinet 28%/50%; board 50%/48%; plaque 59%/42%; cart 13%/63%. New installations follow 4 m modules, with matching shortened corners. These percentages are image guides, not placement transforms. Read Asset proposal for materials, source files and fitting limits.
items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / compositing.
Asset type: environment dressing proposal painted directly onto a real Unreal gameplay screenshot for Total (in)Sanitation.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and controls the exact camera, lens, architecture, perspective, framing, material scale, light fixtures and pixelated first-person hands. Edit this screenshot itself; do not reconstruct a similar corridor.
Primary request: fill selected empty wall and ceiling-edge areas of this existing basement junction with a coherent, production-feasible 1970s pharmaceutical-company service environment, semi-realistic with restrained stylization. The corporate service layer is neglected and dungeon-like, but remains an institutional basement.
Add only these planned assets:
N01: two modest utility pipes along the upper LEFT wall/ceiling edge, following that wall into the junction and turning toward the long corridor on the right. One chipped cream-painted pipe, one dark oxidized steel pipe, industrial elbows, bolted flanges, periodic simple black iron triangular support brackets. Fit the repeated 4 m wall/ceiling panels rather than changing them.
N02: a slim galvanized electrical conduit run at the upper RIGHT corridor edge, with simple junction boxes and regular clamps.
N03: one shallow olive-gray 1970s electrical service cabinet with two doors, a single circular analog meter and small warning label on the large illuminated LEFT wall. Approximate real size 80 cm wide, 100 cm tall, 18 cm deep; mounted at adult chest height. Scuffed enamel edges, selective seam rust, no screens.
N04: a small cream/olive directional enamel plaque at the entrance of the long corridor, above eye height; simple arrow and readable 'EQUIPMENT'. Keep it small and utilitarian.
N05: a narrow dark painted-steel maintenance notice panel with 2-3 yellowed paper work orders, on the CENTRAL pier face facing the viewer, away from the opening edges. No cork or fancy wood.
R01 reuse: one compact gray open plastic janitor cart with a rectangular bucket and two small front compartments, parked tight against the far left branch wall, outside the walking route. It is a reused existing prop shape, not a large hotel trolley.
V01 surface variant: a subdued faded olive institutional paint band approximately 1.1 m high along the existing lower walls, with sparse chipped edges showing the SAME existing concrete/brick beneath. Leave most original wall texture and every architectural edge intact. Mineral streaks occur only below pipe joints; a little dirt along wall bases, no blanket rust or rubbish carpet.
Materials: existing rough masonry/concrete, muted olive/cream enamel, galvanized and dark iron metal, restrained oxide, gray worn plastic, paper labels. Chunky simple readable forms and medium texture detail consistent with the screenshot. Medieval accents only in the pointed forged support brackets; no medieval architecture.
Constraints: KEEP the exact image size/aspect, camera, walls, ceiling slab grid, junction geometry, openings, floor plane, light locations, exposure mood, distant warm shop glimpse and both pixelated hands unchanged. Preserve the original dim lighting with matched local shadows for added props. Keep the central floor and all corridor mouths empty and visibly traversable. Place assets as additive modular dressings; no new recesses or cuts. No new doors, arches, stairs, torches, characters, weapons, giant ductwork, neon, digital displays, volumetric cinematic fog, extreme photorealism, annotation numbers, title, border or watermark.

Targeted revisions:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is the edit target, a finished basement junction concept. Input image 2 is a native thumbnail of the EXISTING janitor cart mesh and controls its shape. Make ONLY ONE localized correction in image 1: replace the small tall two-tier trolley parked far LEFT with the actual squat existing prop design shown in image 2. That existing design is a low gray open rectangular plastic rear tub, a single attached lower front rectangular caddy with two small square compartments, two small circular front fasteners, simple chunky feet/casters. It is around knee height, no upright frame, no overhead tray, no broom, no spray bottles, no towel. Keep it tight against the same left wall and outside the route, with matching dim light/contact shadows. Preserve ABSOLUTELY EVERYTHING ELSE in image 1: identical framing, aspect, camera, geometry, hands, original textures, lights, pipe designs, cabinet, notice board, equipment sign and floor. Do not add anything else. No labels, borders or watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit. In this finished basement junction image change ONLY the material of the squat small janitor cart at far LEFT under the electrical cabinet. Its current subtle gray checkerboard is a preview placeholder and must be replaced with solid neutral warm-gray scuffed rough molded plastic, with sparse realistic grime at edges. Keep the cart's exact current low shape, dimensions, position, open rear tub, small front caddy, fasteners and dark casters unchanged. Preserve every other pixel and all scene objects, framing, architecture, camera, lighting, paint bands, pipework, signs, floor and pixelated hands. Absolutely no other additions or redesign. No labels, border or watermark.

items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / compositing.
Asset type: modular environment dressing concept directly on native Unreal gameplay, Total (in)Sanitation.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: exact camera, floor, walls, ceiling joints, fluorescent locations, first-person pixelated hands and distant shop opening must remain unchanged.
Input image 2 is supporting STYLE and ASSET CONTINUITY only. It shows the previous junction on this SAME route. Continue its small cream and dark iron pipes, narrow right-hand electrical conduit, faded olive lower wall band and restrained 1970s institutional mood. Do not copy its junction, cabinet, cart, notices, camera or composition into target 1.
Primary request: dress this long utilitarian basement corridor so it feels like the neglected service infrastructure of a 1970s pharmaceutical company, semi-realistic and stylized to the same medium detail as the real screenshot.
Planned additions:
N01: the SAME two utility pipes as image 2, along the upper LEFT wall just below the ceiling, in simple repeated 4 m lengths with bolted couplers, a bend and sparse simple triangular black iron brackets. One chipped cream enamel pipe, one dark oxidized steel pipe. At middle distance on the LEFT, include a short vertical branch and small faded red valve wheel; mineral streak only below that joint.
N02: one narrow galvanized electrical conduit on the upper RIGHT wall, periodic square junction boxes and clips aligned to 4 m modules. Keep the ceiling concrete panels and every fluorescent completely unobscured.
N06: one compact wall-mounted manual hose reel below the left-hand pipe branch, at waist height in the middle foreground, approximate diameter 55 cm, projection under 25 cm. Simple olive painted steel circular cheeks, dark gray coiled rubber hose, dull brass nozzle. Short hose end stays in its wall clip, never across the floor.
N04: one small cream/olive 'SERVICE' enamel plaque on the RIGHT wall at eye height, plus a tiny worn utility caution label near the left valve. Clean readable institutional graphics, no new large typography.
V01: continue the same worn muted olive lower wall paint band at 1.1 m, sparse chips revealing the existing concrete/brick. Keep original wall textures and UV scale, do not resurface or rebuild the walls.
Add only a small localized matte damp stain below the valve and dust near wall bases. Keep the entire central floor clear, no drain cuts, puddle lake, scattered props or new corridor branches.
Materials: existing concrete/masonry, reused dark steel/oxide blend, galvanized metal, cream/olive enamel variants, rough rubber and a small brass nozzle. Color and wear match image 2, no orange full-scene grade.
Constraints: This is an additive edit of image 1, preserve exact scene geometry, camera/FOV/perspective, aspect ratio, current light fixture count and positions, low-key exposure, distant warm shop glimpse, and original hands. No taller ceiling, arches, doors, torchlight, digital technology, large ducts, characters, skulls, weapons or clutter. Medieval accent only in the little forged triangular brackets; all services look plausible and human-scale. No annotation numbers, border, title or watermark.

Targeted revision:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this existing finished corridor concept. Change ONLY the cream enamel sign on the RIGHT WALL: keep its shape, position, material, bolts, aging and word 'SERVICE' exactly; remove the black directional arrow next to SERVICE, replacing just that arrow area with matching aged cream enamel. No other changes anywhere. Preserve identical framing/aspect, camera, all original architecture, pipework, left valve and hose reel, conduit, lighting, hands, paint band, floor and distant opening. No new text, labels, border or watermark.

items.title: C / Shop arrival — generated dressing proposal
items.alt: Generated shop dressing retaining the original serving window and spike grille, adding overhead service runs, collection plaque and a right-wall supply station
items.body:
**Owner accepted this direction for modeling on 12 November 2026. Meshes remain unimplemented/unreviewed.**

**AI CONCEPT / not an engine implementation.** Uses the new gameplay capture after walking down the existing stairs. The shop's EQUIPMENT sign, bars, counter and warm task light are existing Pass 01 work.

**NEW:** N01 upper-wall pipe pair; N02 conduit on the right; N04 COLLECTION plaque above the left spike grille; N05 work-order board on the right; N07 two shelf containers and one floor-side bin. **REUSE:** R02 SM_LabShelf below the work orders. Its native asset thumbnail was supplied to the generator. **VARIANT:** V01 olive paint band on side walls.

**Locate the props:** COLLECTION 22%/38%; board 81%/39%; shelf/supply containers 81%/54%; gray bin 83%/66%. The serving opening, spike delivery opening, right door and their floor approaches remain clear. No NPC or interaction design is proposed.
items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / compositing.
Asset type: environment dressing concept directly on actual Unreal gameplay, Total (in)Sanitation.
Inputs: image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and exact geometry/camera authority. Image 2 is supporting style continuity from the upstairs junction on this same route; copy only its materials, small service pipe/conduit design and muted olive 1.1 m lower-wall paint band. Image 3 is a native thumbnail of an EXISTING reusable wall shelf; it controls the shelf's simple shape: one narrow dark tray with raised small edges, two slim upright posts, a top horizontal tube/rail, two small square mounting plates. It is not a large freestanding shelf.
Primary request: furnish the remaining blank wall areas around this 1970s pharmaceutical-company basement equipment counter. The central serving window, the left spike delivery grille and right barred door MUST stay fully usable and retain their exact geometry. The existing grimy masonry and spikes provide the dungeon-like accent. Keep the warm task-light destination.
Add:
N01: the same modest cream-painted and dark iron utility pipe pair from image 2, running tightly at the top wall/ceiling boundary, along the RIGHT side wall then around above the shop facade, with bolted joints and small triangular iron brackets. Do not cross or hide any bars, sign or fluorescent.
N02: one narrow galvanized conduit with a small junction box near the upper RIGHT side wall.
N04: one small cream enamel plaque with 'COLLECTION' mounted on the SOLID wall above the LEFT spike delivery opening. Keep the original centered 'EQUIPMENT' shop sign and its lettering unchanged. No sign inside or covering either opening.
N05: a small dark steel-backed maintenance/work order board with two yellowed paper notices on the blank RIGHT SIDE WALL, beyond the barred door, roughly at eye level. All papers lie within the board outline.
R02: reuse the exact simple wall shelf design from image 3 on that RIGHT SIDE WALL BELOW the notices, away from the door, with one shallow tray and simple tube posts. Place only two small opaque cream/olive cleaning-supply containers on it, no bottles full of glowing liquid or laboratory equipment. Human-scale, about 1 m wide, maximum projection 30 cm. Its posts, small plates and tray use existing metal/paint materials.
R01 reuse: a single low rectangular worn gray plastic cleaning bucket tucked below the right-hand shelf and against the wall. No trolley, mop, broom or new cleaning tools.
V01: continue a restrained faded olive lower-wall paint band along the side walls only, around 1.1 m high, chipped lightly to the SAME underlying masonry. Do not paint over the shop's bars, spike mechanism, center metal shutter or sign. Limit grime to seams and wall bases.
Materials: worn olive/cream enamel, dark iron and selective oxide, galvanized conduit, neutral worn plastic, faded paper. Medium detail and chunky readable forms consistent with the original game. Existing architecture remains the visual anchor, no ornamental redesign.
Hard constraints: preserve exact camera, aspect ratio, perspective, floor, concrete ceiling panel grid, wall corners, height, opening sizes, entire counter, left pointed bars, right barred door, original light positions and original pixelated hands. Match existing warm local shop lighting and dim side-wall illumination; add only contact shadows for additions. All serving/delivery floor approaches stay empty. No NPC, new doorway, arch, torch, castle decoration, huge pipes, new screens, cables on floor, scattered trash or cinematic fog. No annotation numbers, title, border or watermark.
